title: Marriage Is Not a Private Matter

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If a man commits adultery with another man's wife — with the wife of his neighbour — both the adulterer and the adulteress are to be put to death. If a man has sexual relations with his father's wife, he has dishonoured his father. Both the man and the woman are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.'" - Lev 20:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice one thing immediately: both. Both the adulterer and the adulteress. The same penalty for the man and the woman.

That was not how the ancient world worked. In most surrounding cultures, a woman bore the consequences and a man walked away. God refuses that double standard. There is no version of this where the man's part is treated as less.

We still live with the residue of that unfairness. A man's affair is described as a mistake; a woman's is a scandal. The language is different, the sympathy is different, and the church has not always been innocent here.

But look at the seriousness God attaches to marriage. Adultery is not a private arrangement between consenting adults. It reaches into a household, wounds a spouse, marks children, and fractures a community.

Hebrews carries the same weight into the New Testament: Marriage should be honoured by all, and the marriage bed kept pure, for God will judge the adulterer and all the sexually immoral (Heb 13:4).

And yet — when a woman caught in adultery was thrown at Jesus' feet, He did not condemn her. Neither do I condemn you, he said. Go now and leave your life of sin (John 8:11). Both halves of that sentence are the gospel.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you apply the same standard to men and women in these matters?
2. Do you treat marriage — yours or others' — as seriously as God does?
3. What does Jesus' response to the woman in John 8 mean to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You hold everyone to the same standard and that You judge fairly. Guard my heart, honour my commitments, and thank You for the mercy Christ offers. Amen.
